goal: Locate single-month volume anomalies in offline_data/regional_sales.csv by computing each region×product_line monthly sales volume as a multiple of its own 24-month mean, report the top-3 combinations with their multiples and corresponding-month return rates, judge whether each spike is genuine demand or channel stuffing, and save a fully-sourced Markdown report to disk.

plan.title: Inspect CSV structure: Read offline_data/regional_sales.csv: list all column names, total row count, date range (min/max of the month column), and print first 5 rows as sample

Compute monthly volume anomaly ratios: Write and execute Python code: for each (region, product_line) group, compute the 24-month rolling mean of monthly sales volume, then compute the ratio of each month's volume to that rolling mean. Identify the top-3 (region, product_line, month) combinations with the highest ratio. Also extract the return_rate for those specific months. Save intermediate results to a CSV file.

Assess demand vs channel stuffing: Write and execute Python code: for the top-3 anomaly combinations, compute additional diagnostic metrics (e.g., return rate trend before/after the spike month, volume in the 2 months before and after the spike, comparison of return rate to the group's 24-month average return rate) to help judge whether the spike looks like genuine demand or channel stuffing. Save diagnostic results to a CSV.

Write Markdown report: Write a comprehensive Markdown report file saved to disk. The report must include: (1) a level-1 title, (2) at least one data table showing the top-3 combinations with their ratio, month, and return rate, (3) every key number annotated with its source in the format '（来源：offline_data/regional_sales.csv 的 <列名>，<聚合口径与样本行数>）' or '（来源：由前述两行计算）' for derived values, (4) a concluding paragraph at the end judging whether each spike is more likely genuine demand or channel stuffing. Save the report as a .md file and output its absolute path.
